lecturas.subtitulo: Un perro, un taco y un plan que sale mal

capitulos.texto:
Wero is a small white dog. Every morning he sits outside the taco stand and waits.

"How's it going?" says Don Beto, the man who makes the tacos.

Wero moves his tail. He cannot talk, but he can wait. He waits and waits. A boy walks by with a taco in one hand and a large soda in the other. The taco smells like heaven.

The boy drops the taco. It falls on the floor. Wero looks at it. He looks at the boy. He looks at the taco again.

"That's it?" the boy says. "My taco?"

Wero does not move. He is a good dog. He waits.

"You can have it," says the boy. "Don't get worked up. I'll get another one."

Wero eats the taco in two bites. To make a long story short, Wero now has a new friend.

The next day the boy comes back. His name is Tono.

"I'd like a word with you," Tono says to the dog, very serious. Wero sits down.

"You ate my taco. So now you work for me. Deal?"

Wero puts one paw on Tono's shoe.

"Let me know for sure," says Tono, laughing.

Wero barks once. That means yes.

Every day after school, Tono walks to the taco stand and Wero is already there. Don Beto says the dog knows the time better than a clock. He does it on purpose, Tono thinks. He knows exactly when I get out.

One day Tono is sick and cannot come. Wero waits all afternoon. When Tono finally arrives the next day, the dog runs to him.

"If you ever need me, I'll be there in a heartbeat," says Tono.

Wero already knew that. Dogs always know.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué Wero espera afuera del puesto de tacos?
opciones: Porque espera que caiga un taco
Porque le tiene miedo a Don Beto
preguntas.porque: Wero espera todos los días a que alguien tire comida.

preguntas.pregunta: "To make a long story short" en la historia significa…
opciones: Para no hacerte el cuento largo
preguntas.porque: Se usa para saltar los detalles y llegar al final.

preguntas.pregunta: Cuando Tono dice "I'll be there in a heartbeat", promete…
opciones: Que llegará volando, sin tardarse nada
Que va a llamar por teléfono
preguntas.porque: In a heartbeat es al instante, en lo que late el corazón.

lecturas.subtitulo: Wero y Tono suben a la azotea

capitulos.texto:
It is Friday night. Tono cannot sleep, so he goes up to the roof with Wero.

The city is loud. Somewhere a dog barks. Somewhere a TV is on too loud.

"My mom says we could pawn the TV," Tono says. "She says it every month and she never does it."

Wero puts his head on Tono's leg.

"Don't get worked up," says Tono, copying his mother's voice. "Let me soothe your nerves."

Wero closes his eyes.

Above them there are almost no stars, because the city has too many lights. But there are three, and Tono finds all three.

"My grandma said everything is already decided up there. It's written in the stars, she said."

Wero does not answer. He is a dog. But he stays. He always stays.

"See you tomorrow, man," Tono whispers, and falls asleep on the roof with his hand on the dog's back.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué casi no se ven estrellas?
opciones: Porque la ciudad tiene demasiadas luces
preguntas.porque: El texto dice que la ciudad tiene demasiadas luces.

preguntas.pregunta: "It's written in the stars" quiere decir que algo…
preguntas.porque: Es la idea de que el destino ya estaba decidido.

preguntas.pregunta: "Let me soothe your nerves" se usa para…
preguntas.porque: Soothe es calmar, tranquilizar.

lecturas.subtitulo: Lunes, nueve de la mañana, y nadie contesta

capitulos.texto:
Monday morning. My boss drops a message in the group chat and nobody answers for six minutes.

"We're brainstorming at ten," it says. "Everyone on camera."

Dave writes back first, like always. Then Ana. Then the intern, who writes "ok" and nothing else, which somehow makes it worse.

I stare at my screen. My deadline is Friday and I have opened the same file four times without writing anything.

At ten the call starts. My boss shares his screen. Gather the data first, he says, then we talk. There are twelve slides and the eleventh one has my name on it.

"If Carl wants to step up, now is the moment," he says.

Carl does not want to step up. Carl has his camera off.

So I unmute.

"I'm able to take the second half," I say. "But my full intentions are to hand it off to Ana in two weeks. She wrote most of it."

Silence. The kind of silence where you cannot tell if you just helped yourself or ended your career.

Then my boss says: "On behalf of all of us, thank you." And he means it, which is somehow worse.

Ana sends me a private message: two key points to lock in before Friday, and a coffee emoji.

Road to a million, I think. Not now, though. Right now it is just Monday, and I have eleven slides to fix.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace el narrador en la junta?
opciones: Ofrece tomar la segunda mitad del trabajo
preguntas.porque: Dice "I'm able to take the second half".

preguntas.pregunta: "On behalf of all of us" se traduce como…
preguntas.porque: On behalf of es en nombre de, de parte de.

preguntas.pregunta: "Not now, though" al final indica que…
opciones: Ese sueño no es para hoy
preguntas.porque: Though al final suaviza: es un pero, no un nunca.

lecturas.subtitulo: El recibo de la luz y una conversación incómoda

capitulos.texto:
The landlord calls on a Tuesday, which is never good.

"I'd like a word with you," he says. Nobody says that when they are about to give you money.

The heating has been off for eleven days. Eleven. I counted, because my sister keeps asking me to put the heat back on, no? like it is a switch I am refusing to press out of cruelty.

"So you make minimum wage," he says, reading something. "And you are two weeks late."

"I know."

"I am not the bad guy here."

But it is what it is. I have heard that sentence so many times this year that it has stopped meaning anything.

My sister says we could pawn the TV. She has said it every winter since we moved in and we have never done it, because then the apartment would be cold and quiet, and cold is survivable but quiet is not.

On Thursday I call him back.

"I have to draw a line," I tell him. "Heat first, then the late fee. Not the other way around."

He is quiet for a long time.

"Fine," he says. "Friday."

I hang up and my hands are shaking, which is stupid, because I won. But we have to stick together in this building, and next month it will be somebody else's turn to make that call.

The heat comes back on Friday at four in the afternoon. My sister does not say thank you. She just turns the TV on louder, which is the same thing.

Save myself a lot of trouble, I think, if I had just called on day one.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué consigue el narrador al final?
opciones: Que vuelva la calefacción antes de pagar el recargo
preguntas.porque: Pone la condición: calefacción primero, recargo después.

preguntas.pregunta: "I have to draw a line" significa…
preguntas.porque: Draw a line es poner un límite en una negociación.

preguntas.pregunta: "But it is what it is" se usa cuando…
opciones: Algo no se puede cambiar y hay que aceptarlo
Algo es exactamente lo que se pidió
preguntas.porque: Es la resignación: es lo que hay.

lecturas.subtitulo: Cuarenta minutos y una pregunta que no esperabas

capitulos.texto:
The recruiter looks at my resume for a long time before she says anything.

"Tell me about the one you are proudest of."

My flagship project, then. Eleven months, four people, a pipeline that moved data from thirteen hundred stores into one place every night. I say the word we a lot, because it was true.

"And you had full command of the architecture?"

"Full command, no. I owned the reconciliation side."

She writes something down. I cannot tell if honesty just cost me the job.

"Walk me through grading metrics before deployment."

That one I can answer in my sleep.

Then, near the end:

"If you don't mind me asking? Why are you leaving?"

There is a version of this answer that is safe and boring. I have practiced it. Growth, new challenges, the usual.

I do not use it.

"I'm able to do the work there for another five years and nothing would change," I say. "But my full intentions are to build something people actually use."

She smiles for the first time in forty minutes.

"I love that you're pivoting," she says. "Most people say growth and I stop listening."

I get the call two days later. Trustworthy, she wrote in her notes. I asked.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué la reclutadora sonríe?
opciones: Porque el candidato dio la respuesta segura
Porque dijo la verdad en vez del discurso ensayado
preguntas.porque: Ella misma dice que deja de escuchar cuando oye la respuesta de siempre.

preguntas.pregunta: "If you don't mind me asking?" sirve para…
preguntas.porque: Es la fórmula educada antes de una pregunta personal.

preguntas.pregunta: Decir "Full command, no" en una entrevista es…
opciones: Reconocer un límite, y aquí juega a favor
preguntas.porque: La historia trata justamente de que la honestidad le funcionó.

lecturas.subtitulo: Una amistad que se estira y no se rompe

capitulos.texto:
"I'm drifting away from you guys," Nacho says, and nobody argues, which is the worst part.

He moved across the city in March. Forty minutes on the metro. That is all it took.

"You could come on Sundays," says Ale.

"I work Sundays."

"Then Saturdays."

"I'm breaking the habit of smoking and if I come here I smoke." He laughs when he says it, but it is not a joke.

Ale gets loud. Nacho gets quiet. That is how it always goes with them.

"Stop screaming at me," Nacho says finally.

And Ale stops. That is new.

Two hours later we are still on the roof and nobody has left.

"I went through with it," Nacho says. "The job. I start Monday."

"You didn't tell us."

"I'm telling you now."

Ale opens his mouth, closes it, opens it again.

"I have to draw a line somewhere," Nacho says. "I can't be here three nights a week and be there at seven."

"Us first, like always," Ale says, and it sounds like a joke and it is not.

But Nacho comes back the next Saturday anyway, and the one after that.

"Thanks for the rides," he says every time, getting out of the car at midnight. Eight months later he is still saying it, and we are still driving him.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué decide Nacho al final?
opciones: Dejar de ver a sus amigos
preguntas.porque: Vuelve el sábado siguiente y el siguiente.

preguntas.pregunta: "I'm drifting away from you guys" describe…
opciones: Alejarse poco a poco, sin querer
preguntas.porque: Drift away es irse alejando solo, como una corriente.

preguntas.pregunta: "I went through with it" significa…
opciones: Lo llevé a cabo, no me eché para atrás
preguntas.porque: Go through with it es cumplir algo que costaba trabajo decidir.

lecturas.titulo: El día que Wero se perdió
lecturas.subtitulo: Tres calles, una tienda y un perro asustado

capitulos.texto:
Tono opens the door and forgets to close it.

"Shut the door!" his mother says, but it is too late. Wero is already outside.

The dog runs three streets. Then he stops. Nothing smells like home anymore.

A woman with a bag of oranges looks at him.

"You are lost, little one."

Wero sits down. When you are lost, sitting is the smartest thing a dog can do.

Tono runs out of the house. He looks under cars. He asks at the taco stand. Don Beto has not seen him.

"Let me know for sure if he comes back," says Tono, almost crying.

"Do not despair," says Don Beto. "That dog knows this street better than you do."

Two hours later Wero walks home by himself, slowly, like nothing happened.

"Don't push your luck," Tono tells him, hugging him too hard.

Wero does it again the next month.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Cómo regresa Wero a la casa?
preguntas.porque: El texto dice que camina de regreso él solo, dos horas después.

preguntas.pregunta: "Don't push your luck" se le dice a alguien que…
preguntas.porque: Es la advertencia de no abusar de la buena suerte.

preguntas.pregunta: "Do not despair" quiere decir…
preguntas.porque: Despair es desesperarse, perder la esperanza.

lecturas.subtitulo: Un perro mojado y una tarde sin salir

capitulos.texto:
It rains all afternoon. Wero hates the rain.

He sits by the window and watches the water. Every few minutes he looks at Tono, like Tono could turn it off.

"Don't get worked up," says Tono. "It always stops."

Tono's mother comes home wet and tired. She sits down and does not move for ten minutes.

"This heat drains your energy," she said this morning. Now it is cold and she is tired anyway. Some days are just like that.

Tono makes her a coffee. It is not very good. She drinks all of it.

"Let me soothe your nerves," he says, copying her voice, and she laughs for the first time since Monday.

The rain stops at seven. Wero stands up immediately, like he knew.

"Another one doesn't hurt," says his mother, holding out her cup.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace Tono por su mamá?
preguntas.porque: Le prepara un café que no le queda muy bueno.

preguntas.pregunta: "This heat drains your energy" significa que el calor…
preguntas.porque: Drain es drenar, vaciar.

preguntas.pregunta: "Another one doesn't hurt" se usa para…
preguntas.porque: Es la forma de pedir otro sin pedirlo directamente.

lecturas.subtitulo: Wero encuentra algo que no debía

capitulos.texto:
Wero finds a keychain under the couch. It is small, it is shiny, and it is not his.

"Give it here," says Tono.

Wero runs. Wero always runs.

"Imma rip your keychain off," Tono's older sister yells from the kitchen, which is not even the right expression, but she is angry and it is her keychain.

They chase the dog around the table four times.

"Shut the door!" says their mother, who has said that sentence nine thousand times in her life.

Wero drops the keychain by himself, in the middle of the room, and sits next to it.

"It's a collectible," says the sister, picking it up. "My friend brought it from Monterrey."

"That's it?" says Tono. "All of that for a keychain?"

Wero moves his tail. For him it was a great afternoon.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿De quién es el llavero?
preguntas.porque: La hermana lo reclama desde la cocina y luego lo recoge.

preguntas.pregunta: "It's a collectible" quiere decir que la cosa es…
preguntas.porque: Collectible es un objeto de colección.

preguntas.pregunta: "That's it?" se usa cuando…
opciones: Algo resultó menos de lo esperado
preguntas.porque: Es la decepción: ¿eso es todo?

lecturas.subtitulo: Un enemigo nuevo, del tamaño de un zapato

capitulos.texto:
There is a cat on the roof next door. Gray, small, and completely sure of himself.

Every morning at seven the cat walks along the wall, very slowly, right in front of Wero.

"He does it on purpose," says Tono.

Wero barks. The cat does not even look at him. That is the worst part.

One Saturday the cat sits down on the wall and stays there for an hour. Wero sits below and stays there too. Neither one moves.

"Do not despair," Tono tells his dog, laughing.

At noon the cat jumps down into the yard, walks past Wero without hurrying, drinks from his water bowl, and leaves.

Wero does nothing. Absolutely nothing.

"It could have fooled me," says Tono's sister from the window. "I thought he was brave."

The next morning at seven, they are both back on the wall.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace Wero cuando el gato baja?
preguntas.porque: El texto dice que no hace absolutamente nada.

preguntas.pregunta: "He does it on purpose" significa que lo hace…
preguntas.porque: On purpose es a propósito, con intención.

preguntas.pregunta: "It could have fooled me" se dice cuando…
preguntas.porque: Es un comentario irónico: pues me tenía engañado.

lecturas.subtitulo: La hermana de Tono y una decisión de las diez de la noche

capitulos.texto:
At ten at night, Tono's sister decides to cut her own hair.

"Get your hair done," their mother told her last week. "With a professional. Please."

She did not.

Tono watches from the door with the dog. Neither of them says anything, because both of them know better.

First she cuts the left side. Then she cuts the right side, to make it even. Then the left side again.

"Your bangs," says Tono, very quietly.

"I know."

"That's it?" he asks, when she puts down the scissors.

She looks in the mirror for a long time. Wero looks at her too, with his head to one side.

"You look fly," says Tono, and he means it, because she is his sister and because it is eleven at night and nobody can fix anything now.

She laughs. Then she cries a little. Then she laughs again.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué le había dicho la mamá?
opciones: Que se cortara el pelo ella misma
preguntas.porque: Le dijo get your hair done, con un profesional.

preguntas.pregunta: "You look fly" es un…
preguntas.porque: Fly aquí es que te ves muy bien.

preguntas.pregunta: "Your bangs" se refiere a…
preguntas.porque: Bangs es el fleco.

lecturas.subtitulo: Cinco chavos, un balón y un perro que no juega

capitulos.texto:
Five kids, one ball, and a roof that is too small for both teams.

Tono is the goalkeeper because he is the slowest. Nobody says it like that, but everybody knows.

Wero watches from the corner. He never chases the ball. Not once, in three years.

"That's the weird part about me," Tono says when they ask why his dog does not play. "My dog is lazier than I am."

The game ends two to two, which means they need a tiebreaker, which means somebody has to shoot from the water tank.

Tono shoots. The ball goes over the wall and into the street.

Silence.

"We gonna put it all together tomorrow," says Ale, who says that about everything.

They go down to look for the ball. Wero goes first, like he always does when everybody finally decides to move.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué Tono es el portero?
preguntas.porque: El texto lo dice: es el más lento y todos lo saben.

preguntas.pregunta: "Tiebreaker" es…
preguntas.porque: Tie es empate y breaker lo rompe.

preguntas.pregunta: "That's the weird part about me" introduce…
preguntas.porque: Es la forma de presentar la propia rareza.

lecturas.subtitulo: Cuatro pisos y una llave que no aparece

capitulos.texto:
The elevator has been broken since February and it is now June.

I meet the neighbor from 4B on the stairs, both of us carrying groceries, both of us pretending we are not out of breath.

"I was locked out of your room once," she says, which makes no sense until I remember she used to sublet the place before me.

"The lock still sticks."

"It always did."

On the third floor somebody is playing music too loud and somebody else is yelling about it.

"Don't slam the door," she says to nobody in particular, and we both laugh, because in this building that sentence is a joke.

At my floor she stops.

"We can swing by his house on Sunday," she says. "The administrator. Four of us. He answers when there are four of us."

I say yes. Four is not many, but it is more than one.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué proponen hacer el domingo?
opciones: Ir en grupo con el administrador
preguntas.porque: Ella propone pasar a casa del administrador entre cuatro.

preguntas.pregunta: "We can swing by his house" es…
preguntas.porque: Swing by es pasar de rápido por un lugar.

preguntas.pregunta: "I was locked out" significa que…
opciones: Se quedó afuera sin poder entrar
preguntas.porque: Locked out es quedarse fuera, normalmente sin llave.

lecturas.subtitulo: Doña Lupe, su porche y una lección que nadie pidió

capitulos.texto:
Doña Lupe is always in the same place.

"Sittin' on my porch, knitting," she says, when anybody asks what she did today. She has been saying it for eleven years.

Last winter she taught my sister. Two afternoons a week, no charge, no lessons, just sitting there until something worked.

"I wanna knit," I told her once, half joking.

"So knit."

"I don't have time."

She looked at me the way people look at you when they have already decided you are wrong.

"It's a matter of you wanting to," she said, and went back to her hands.

That was in November. In March I bought the needles. In April I made something that was almost a scarf.

"It's a collectible," said my sister, holding it up. She was being cruel and she was also right.

Doña Lupe never said anything about it. She just moved over on the step so I could sit down.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace Doña Lupe cuando el narrador aprende a tejer?
opciones: No dice nada y le hace lugar
preguntas.porque: Solo se recorre en el escalón para que se siente.

preguntas.pregunta: "It's a matter of you wanting to" quiere decir…
opciones: Es cuestión de que tú quieras
preguntas.porque: A matter of es cuestión de.

preguntas.pregunta: "I wanna knit" es la forma hablada de…
preguntas.porque: Wanna es la reducción de want to.

lecturas.subtitulo: Una contraseña débil y una conversación incómoda

capitulos.texto:
The kid from 2A knocks on my door on a Tuesday.

"Your security is kind of off," he says, before hello.

"My what?"

"Your wifi. The password is the name of the building and the year. Everyone on this floor is on it."

I stand there with the door half open.

"How do you know that?"

"I've been hammerin' at these things all summer. It's a hobby."

He is sixteen. His hobby is breaking into things and then telling people about it, which is somehow both a crime and a favor.

"Change it now," he says. "Don't push that off to later. Later means never."

So I change it while he stands there, and he reads the new one over my shoulder and shakes his head.

"Better. Not good. Better."

Then he goes back downstairs to tell 2C.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace el chavo después de avisarle al narrador?
opciones: Va a avisarle a otro vecino
preguntas.porque: Baja a decirle lo mismo a 2C.

preguntas.pregunta: "Push that off to later" significa…
preguntas.porque: Push off es posponer.

preguntas.pregunta: "Your security is kind of off" quiere decir que…
opciones: La seguridad está apagada por completo
preguntas.porque: Kind of off es medio mal, no del todo apagado.

lecturas.subtitulo: Tres meses para caerle bien a un equipo

capitulos.texto:
The new guy does not talk for four days.

On the fifth, in the middle of a meeting where nobody asked him anything, he says: "Ain't good with people. Sorry. I'll get there."

Nobody knows what to do with that, so we move on.

He is very good. That becomes obvious in week two, when he finds a bug that three of us had walked past for a month.

"I gotta give you props," says Ana, and he goes red and looks at his screen.

By week eight he eats lunch with us. By week twelve he argues in meetings, which is how you know somebody has stopped being new.

"Now we have built trust," he says one Friday, half joking, raising a paper cup.

It is a strange sentence. It is also exactly right, and none of us would have said it out loud.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Cómo se nota que el nuevo ya dejó de ser nuevo?
preguntas.porque: El texto dice que así se sabe: cuando empieza a discutir.

preguntas.pregunta: "I gotta give you props" es…
preguntas.porque: Give props es reconocer el mérito de alguien.

preguntas.pregunta: "Ain't good with people" es inglés…
preguntas.porque: Ain't es muy común al hablar, pero no se escribe en un correo de trabajo.

lecturas.subtitulo: Noventa minutos que cabían en diez

capitulos.texto:
"If I could just have everybody's attention," says the director, at minute forty of a meeting scheduled for thirty.

Four people unmute at the same time. Nobody speaks. Then everybody speaks.

"Please, go on," says the director, to all four at once, which helps nobody.

I have a document open in another window with the two things I actually need from this call. Both of them take one sentence.

At minute seventy I get one. At minute eighty-eight I get the other, by writing it in the chat where the director cannot see it.

"We'll push that off to later," he says about the third topic, which was the only important one.

Ana sends me a message: two words and a face.

The call ends at ninety-four minutes. I sit for a second before I open anything else, because opening something else right away is how a Tuesday disappears.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué pasa con el tercer tema?
preguntas.porque: El director dice que lo dejan para más tarde.

preguntas.pregunta: "If I could just have everybody's attention" se usa para…
preguntas.porque: Es la fórmula educada para callar a la sala.

preguntas.pregunta: "Please, go on" invita a…
preguntas.porque: Go on es continúa.

lecturas.subtitulo: Un número, dos versiones y una pregunta que nadie contesta

capitulos.texto:
They offer me twelve percent.

"A little bit after taxes," says my manager, "it's less, obviously."

Obviously.

I do the math that night at the kitchen table and the number is smaller than it sounded in the room, which is the whole point of saying it as a percentage.

"Is this what the market pays?" I ask on Thursday.

"That's the golden question."

That is not an answer. He knows it is not an answer. We both sit with it for a second.

"Look," he says finally. "Twelve is what I can sign today. Staying quiet is only gonna get you so far, and you have been very quiet for two years."

That one lands. I have been quiet for two years.

I take the twelve. I also start answering recruiter messages that week, for the first time since I got here.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué hace el narrador al final?
opciones: Lo acepta y empieza a buscar
preguntas.porque: Toma el doce y empieza a contestarles a los reclutadores.

preguntas.pregunta: "That's the golden question" se dice cuando…
opciones: La pregunta es la buena y no hay respuesta
preguntas.porque: Es reconocer que dio en el clavo, casi siempre para no contestar.

preguntas.pregunta: "Only gonna get you so far" quiere decir que algo…
opciones: Te lleva solo hasta cierto punto
preguntas.porque: So far marca un tope, no un cero.

lecturas.subtitulo: Un modelo, dos métricas y una decisión de viernes

capitulos.texto:
"Gather the data first," Ana says. "Then we argue."

So we spend Wednesday and Thursday gathering, and on Friday we argue anyway, because the data does not decide anything by itself. It never does.

The model is better than the old one on nine metrics and worse on one. The one it is worse on is the one that reaches customers.

"We draw the cutoff line at zero point eight," says the lead.

"That drops fourteen percent of real cases."

"And at zero point six we send garbage to four hundred people a day."

Nobody is wrong, which is the worst kind of meeting.

In the end we ship at zero point seven five and write down exactly why, in a document with both names on it.

"Trustworthy," Ana says, looking at the doc. "That's the whole job. Not right. Trustworthy."

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Cómo termina la discusión?
opciones: Se van a un punto intermedio y lo documentan
preguntas.porque: Salen con 0.75 y escriben el porqué con los dos nombres.

preguntas.pregunta: "We draw the cutoff line" es…
preguntas.porque: Cutoff line es el umbral donde se corta.

preguntas.pregunta: Según Ana, el trabajo no es ser correcto sino…
preguntas.porque: Trustworthy es confiable.

lecturas.subtitulo: Seis meses estudiando para una mañana

capitulos.texto:
"Your entrance exam is at seven," my mother says, at five in the morning, standing in my doorway with coffee.

I know. I have known for six months.

On the bus there are forty kids with the same folder. Some of them are reading. Most of them are pretending to read.

The girl next to me has her notes in three colors.

"Well studied," I say, pointing at them.

"Not really. It just looks like it."

That makes me feel better than anything my mother said all week.

The exam is ninety questions. I know maybe seventy. I guess on twelve and I leave eight blank because guessing costs points here.

Outside, afterward, nobody wants to talk about it and everybody talks about it.

"Ambitious," says the girl with the three colors, when I tell her which program I put first.

"Too ambitious?"

"I didn't say that."

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué deja ocho preguntas en blanco?
opciones: Porque se le acabó el tiempo
preguntas.porque: El texto dice que aquí adivinar cuesta puntos.

preguntas.pregunta: "Well studied" aquí es…
preguntas.porque: Le está diciendo que se ve bien preparada.

preguntas.pregunta: "Ambitious" como respuesta corta puede ser…
opciones: Un elogio o una advertencia, según el tono
preguntas.porque: La historia termina justo en esa ambigüedad.

lecturas.subtitulo: Una clase de ocho y una noche que no se planeó

capitulos.texto:
"Are you hungover?" the professor asks, without looking up.

Half the room laughs. The kid in the third row does not.

"A little."

"Then you already know how this goes."

He does. He gets called on four times in fifty minutes, which is more than the whole semester put together.

"I gotta take this on the chin," he says at the break, holding a coffee with both hands like it is medicine.

"You could just not come."

"Then he wins."

That is not really how it works, but at eight in the morning everything feels like a fight.

By the second hour he is answering correctly, which somehow annoys everyone more.

"Gotta chill out on here," he tells us afterward, meaning the parties, meaning Sundays, meaning everything.

He says it again the following Monday.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué pasa en la segunda hora?
preguntas.porque: Contesta correctamente, y eso molesta más a todos.

preguntas.pregunta: "I gotta take this on the chin" significa…
preguntas.porque: Take it on the chin es aguantarse sin quejarse.

preguntas.pregunta: "Are you hungover?" pregunta si…
preguntas.porque: Hungover es la resaca del día siguiente.

lecturas.subtitulo: Una canción, un carro y cuatro personas gritando

capitulos.texto:
Kevin puts on a song nobody has heard and everybody hates for eleven seconds.

Then the chorus hits.

"That's a banger," says Ale, from the back seat, and that is the end of the argument.

We play it four times between the gas station and the house.

Kevin found it in a playlist from a stream at three in the morning. Kevin finds everything at three in the morning, which is why nobody questions where his music comes from anymore.

"Shout out to Kevin," says Nacho, very seriously, like he is on the radio.

Kevin does not answer. He just turns it up.

Later, outside the house, he tells me he has not been sleeping.

"Nobody checked up on me all month," he says. "Except you, Tuesday."

I do not remember what I wrote him on Tuesday. He does. That is usually how it works.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Qué le dice Kevin al narrador afuera de la casa?
opciones: Que se va de la ciudad
preguntas.porque: Le dice que no ha dormido y que casi nadie lo buscó.

preguntas.pregunta: "That's a banger" quiere decir que la canción…
preguntas.porque: Banger es un temazo.

preguntas.pregunta: "Checked up on me" significa que alguien…
opciones: Se preocupó por él, le escribió
preguntas.porque: Check up on someone es ver cómo está alguien.

lecturas.subtitulo: Una discusión que no era sobre lo que parecía

capitulos.texto:
Ale is yelling about a parking spot and it is not about the parking spot.

We all know it. Nacho knows it best, which is why he does not answer.

"Let him trip," Nacho tells me quietly. "He needs it out."

So we stand there in the street for eleven minutes while Ale says eleven minutes of things that are only half about us.

His father has been in the hospital since Thursday. He has not mentioned that once tonight.

When he finally stops, he is out of breath and a little embarrassed.

"Blow off some steam," he says, half apology, half explanation.

"We know."

"You don't know."

"We know about your dad, Ale."

Silence. Then he sits down on the curb, and we sit down too, all four of us, on a street where we are absolutely in the way.

"We don't cut and run," says Nacho. Nobody argues with that one.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿De qué se trataba realmente el pleito?
opciones: Del papá de Ale, que está en el hospital
preguntas.porque: El texto lo dice: su papá lleva en el hospital desde el jueves.

preguntas.pregunta: "Blow off some steam" es…
preguntas.porque: Es soltar la presión acumulada.

preguntas.pregunta: "We don't cut and run" quiere decir…
preguntas.porque: Cut and run es abandonar cuando se pone difícil.

lecturas.subtitulo: Cuarenta minutos de ciudad vacía

capitulos.texto:
At one in the morning the city belongs to whoever is still driving.

Nacho lives forty minutes away now. Every Saturday somebody takes him, and every Saturday he says the same thing getting out of the car.

"Thanks for the rides."

Not ride. Rides. All of them, going back two years.

Tonight it is my turn. We do not talk much. The radio does most of it.

At a red light on an empty avenue he says: "We can swing by his house next week. Kevin's. He's been weird."

"He's been weird since March."

"Yeah."

The light turns green and neither of us moves for a second.

"If he calls you, go," Nacho says.

"I'll be there in a heartbeat."

He nods, gets out, and hits the roof of the car twice, which in this group has meant goodbye since we were seventeen.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿De qué hablan en el semáforo?
preguntas.porque: Nacho propone ir a ver a Kevin, que anda raro.

preguntas.pregunta: ¿Por qué dice "rides" en plural?
opciones: Porque agradece todos los aventones, no solo este
Es un error del inglés hablado
preguntas.porque: El texto lo aclara: todos, de dos años para acá.

preguntas.pregunta: "I'll be there in a heartbeat" promete…
preguntas.porque: In a heartbeat es al instante.
